lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: Okay, I think we're all here. Hi, Juliet. Thanks for making the time.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Hi, Benvolio. Hi, Romeo. Thanks for coming over.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: So, quick intros for the notes. I'm product on the Montague side, Romeo's the staff engineer who'll actually build most of our half.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: And I'm head of product at Capulet, I own the spec on our side. Tybalt, our engineering lead, sent me with a question, so, fair warning.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: Noted. Do you want to walk us through scope?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Yeah. So, short version. Balcony App does field inspections in warehouses. Inspectors walk a site, take photos, log findings, sign the report. Right now that data stops at Balcony. Schema Bridge is a shared format for an inspection record plus a bridge that moves those records into Mesh Routing, so your side can route work off them.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: And the record is the five fields in your draft? I skimmed it this morning.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Right. Site, inspector, photos, findings, signed at. I wrote it this morning, so it's rough.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: No, it's a good start. The part I'd push on is the sync. You've got a nightly batch.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: I do. It felt simple.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: It is simple. But if an inspector signs something at nine in the morning, nobody downstream sees it until the next day. I'd rather we send events. Each signed inspection goes over as its own event, when it's signed. And if one fails it doesn't take the whole night with it.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Huh. Okay. I like that. I'm not attached to the batch, I just didn't want to overbuild.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: Can I jump in on timing? Ducal Freight is the pilot, and I'd love to show them something real soon. What if we aim for a demo this Friday?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: This Friday. Okay. That's, um, ambitious.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: We've got our own release go or no-go Friday morning, but a demo in the afternoon could work. Let's do it.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: Great. I'll set it up with Ducal.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay, so, Tybalt's question. His worry is, if Balcony depends on Mesh Routing, and Mesh Routing goes down, do our inspectors stop working? They can't wait on someone else's service.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Totally fair question. And honestly, he should worry about that, I would.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: So what's the answer?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: A local queue. Balcony doesn't talk to Mesh Routing directly when an inspector signs something. It drops the event into a queue on the device. When Mesh Routing is reachable, the queue drains. When it's not, events just wait. The inspector never knows the difference.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: So Balcony keeps working no matter what's happening on your side.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: That's the idea. Our outage becomes a delay, not a failure.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: I think Tybalt can live with that. He'll want to see it, though.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: I'll prototype it. Give me a couple of days.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: What about the other open question in the doc? Field versioning?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Right. If we add a field to the inspection record, or change one, who decides? Is it us, is it you, is it both?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Hmm. I don't think we should answer that in the first meeting.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: Agreed, let's leave it open. But let's not leave it open forever.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Fair. I'll keep it in the spec as an open question.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: Okay, action items, so we don't lose them. Juliet?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: I'll do a spec v2 by Wednesday. Switch the sync to events, add the local queue, and keep versioning as an open question.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: And I'll prototype the queue.

lines.speaker: benvolio_montague
lines.text: And I'll set up Friday with Ducal. Anything else?

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: No, I think that's good. Thanks, both of you. This was easier than I expected.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Don't tell Tybalt that, he'll get suspicious.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Ha. I'll tell him you answered his question. Talk soon.
